mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X gives N items to Y', immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Treating a transfer as a later adjustment rather than applying it at the point it occurs.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order named on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any direct comparative statement of the form 'A has K more than B'.
mathgap.example: Swapping the sides and writing B = A + K instead of A = B + K.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have', interpret as (A − B) = (C − D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates two "has more than" differences.
mathgap.example: Treating the right‑hand side as an absolute difference or swapping the order of C and D.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement 'A has N items' fixes A's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a plain count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is the initial value even if earlier transfers have already changed it.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and simplify, propagating constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each new assignment or equation resolution.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known variable untouched in later equations, missing simplifications.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and difference equations—to ensure no contradictions.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Once a complete solution has been derived.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution that violates a previously stated transfer.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after earlier statements and transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing statements in the order they appear.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a comparison that occurs after a transfer affecting that person.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through other variables, and solve only that subsystem.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before attempting to solve the full system, to reduce unnecessary work.
mathgap.example: Including unrelated equations that never affect the queried variable, leading to wasted effort.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if the names differ by only a single character (e.g., 'Erich' vs 'Erick'); do not merge them based on similarity.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem contains multiple similarly spelled names.
mathgap.example: Conflating 'Erich' and 'Erick' into a single variable, causing contradictory equations.

mathgap.title: Flexible Comparative Phrase Parsing
mathgap.principle: Recognize that variations of comparative phrasing (e.g., 'has K more onions from X' or 'has K more onions than X') convey the same signed difference and should be parsed as A − B = K.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement that does not exactly match the standard 'has K more than' pattern.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'Ruby has 3 more onions from Fernando' as a direct count (Ruby = 3) instead of a comparison (Ruby − Fernando = 3).

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than"
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model misinterprets the phrase and writes B = A + K instead of A = B + K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of names; treat the statement as A − B = K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes 'has more than' implies a positive difference and takes |A − B|.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the signed difference; do not apply absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model applies all transfers after solving the static equations, missing intermediate updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, before processing later statements.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes the count is fixed from the start, not considering earlier transfers that may have changed it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "has N" as fixing the count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier operations.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model enforces A > B even when the equation yields a negative difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow signed differences; the equation may be negative if the named order implies it.
